title: Opponent wrongly attacks Le Blanc for denying assurance is justifying faith's formal act
source_text: CXV. Porro ex doctrina Scholae Reformatae, hactenus fideliter & syncere deducta, apparet quam immerito & absque ratione, vir ille doctus & disertus, qui nuper scripsit adversus Reformatos, tanquam Christianam Ethicen subvertentes, operis sui libro decimo, capite quarto, aggressus me sit, ut eum qui communem Reformatorum doctrinam deseruerim, Thesibus ante editis, De Certitudine quam quis habere possit & debeat de sua coram Deo justificatione. Idque quia ibi affirmo fiduciam certam atque absolutam de obtenta a Deo remissione peccatorum, & nostra per Christi gratiam reconciliatione, non esse proprium & formalem actum fidei justificantis, ratione cujus sit conditio, vel instrumentum nostrae coram Deo justificationis.
pass_a_gloss: Further, from the doctrine of the Reformed School, thus far faithfully and sincerely drawn out, it appears how undeservedly and without reason that learned and eloquent man, who recently wrote against the Reformed as subverting Christian ethics, in the tenth book, fourth chapter of his work, has attacked me as one who has deserted the common doctrine of the Reformers in theses previously published, On the Certainty which someone can and ought to have concerning his justification before God. And that because there I affirm that certain and absolute trust concerning the remission of sins obtained from God, and our reconciliation through Christ's grace, is not the proper and formal act of justifying faith, by reason of which it is the condition or instrument of our justification before God.
pass_b_english: From the Reformed doctrine just unpacked, that learned opponent who charges the Reformed with subverting Christian ethics attacks me without cause — as if my Certainty theses deserted common Reformed teaching.
His grievance: I deny that certain absolute trust that one's sins are already remitted is justifying faith's proper formal act — the condition or instrument of justification before God.

lemmas.latin: fiduciam certam atque absolutam de obtenta a Deo remissione
lemmas.gloss: certain and absolute trust concerning remission obtained from God
